responses.response: In this workspace, the exact backend subtype is `Container_Api`; `projects/shared/spec-containers.c4` declares `Container_Api`, and there is no declared `Container_API`. `Container` is the generic base kind, but the repository guidance is to use the more specific declared subtype when it fits. For logical-model relationships, `projects/shared/spec-global.c4` declares `uses`, `calls`, `async`, `reads`, and `writes`; toward a database, the precise choices are usually `reads` and `writes`, not invented verbs like `query` or `invokes`. To verify in the active workspace, use `read-project-summary` in a normal LikeC4 workflow, then cross-check `projects/shared/spec-containers.c4` and `projects/shared/spec-global.c4`; `projects/template/system-model.c4` and `projects/spec-showcase/containers.c4` show `api -[reads]-> database` and `api -[writes]-> database`.

Between an app VM and a database VM in deployment, use the deployment taxonomy from `projects/shared/spec-deployment.c4`: `sql` is the better fit when you want a database-specific edge, while `tcp` is valid if you intentionally model only generic transport. Do not use `calls` on the deployment side, because `calls` belongs to the logical-model taxonomy in `projects/shared/spec-global.c4`. In the logical application model, the valid relationship kinds remain `uses`, `calls`, `async`, `reads`, and `writes`; for an app talking to a database, `reads` and `writes` are the most precise, with the protocol recorded in `technology` (for example `SQL` or `PostgreSQL`). To confirm, use `read-project-summary` in a normal workflow and cross-check `projects/shared/spec-deployment.c4` plus `projects/shared/spec-global.c4`; `projects/template/system-model.c4` shows `reads` and `writes` with database technology.

The exact deployment kind for a firewall in this repository is `Infra_Fw`; `projects/shared/spec-deployment.c4` declares `Infra_Fw` and does not declare `Infra_Firewall`. Two nearby valid deployment kinds are `Infra_F5` and `Infra_Router`; `Node_Vm` is also valid if you need a VM rather than a network appliance. To verify in the active workspace, use `read-project-summary` in a normal LikeC4 workflow and cross-check `projects/shared/spec-deployment.c4`.

Start from the source of truth, not memory: in a normal LikeC4 workflow use `read-project-summary`, and in the repository cross-check `projects/shared/spec-containers.c4`. From the declared taxonomy, the exact HTTP API kind is `Container_Api` and the exact message-queue kind is `Container_Queue`. For an async worker, do not guess `Container_Worker`: there is no declared `Container_Worker` in `projects/shared/spec-containers.c4`; the shared spec does declare `Container_ProcessingServer`, and `projects/spec-showcase/containers.c4` uses it as a background job processor fed from `Container_Queue`. When two names look similar, accept only the exact declared identifier and reject the lookalike—for example `Container_Api` is valid and `Container_API` is not—and if no dedicated subtype exists, use the closest declared kind that matches the behavior or fall back to generic `Container` only after verification.

For a web application talking to an API in the logical model, use `calls`, not `https`. In this workspace, the protocol belongs in the relationship `technology` field—for example `webapp -[calls]-> api { technology 'HTTPS' }`—which is exactly how `projects/template/system-model.c4` and `projects/spec-showcase/containers.c4` model it. The relationship kind `https` becomes valid only on deployment-side infrastructure relationships, because `projects/shared/spec-deployment.c4` declares `https` as a deployment relationship while `projects/shared/spec-global.c4` declares `calls` for the logical model. To confirm in the active workspace, use `read-project-summary` in a normal workflow and cross-check those shared specs.
